340900.title: Conjecture on perfect linear hypergraphs and disjoint unions
340900.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph is **linear** if any two edges have at most $1$ vertex in common, and an $r$-uniform hypergraph is **perfect** if its Lagrangian density equals that of the complete $r$-graph on one fewer vertex. For $r$-graphs $G$ and $H$, let $G\bigsqcup H$ denote their disjoint union.

**Perfectness conjecture.** (1) For $r\ge 3$, there exists $n$ such that every linear $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $n$ vertices is perfect. (2) For $r\ge 3$, there exists $n$ such that if $G$ and $H$ are perfect $r$-graphs with at least $n$ vertices, then $G\bigsqcup H$ is perfect.

The conjecture proposes broad classes of perfect hypergraphs, extending the fact that all $2$-graphs are perfect and that most hypergraphs with known Lagrangian densities are perfect. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.
340900.review_depth: Source v1 introduction, definition of forbidden-hypergraph Lagrangian density and perfectness; preliminary Fact2.1–2.3 excerpts.
340900.ordinary_attempt: Disjoint components maximize their OWN homogeneous Lagrangian separately, but target density is a supremum over all forbidden-graph-free hosts. That observation does not compute the density of a forbidden disjoint union.
340900.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need uniform forbidden-host extremal bound for every sufficiently large linear r-graph and disjoint pair. No concrete full mechanism. No primary proof body audit.

370012.title: Spanning-subtree probability conjecture for the complete graph
370012.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $s_k(G)$ be the number of subtrees of $G$ with $k$ vertices, and define the spanning-subtree probability

$$
p(G)=\frac{s_n(G)}{\sum_{k=1}^n s_k(G)}.
$$

**Spanning-subtree probability conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices,

$$
p(G)\le p(K_n).
$$

The source states that this less restrictive conjecture is an open problem and that it would support the extremality of the complete graph.

370012.ordinary_attempt: Source Cor3.4 is exactly p(G)≤p(K_n); sum the displayed lower bounds for every s_j/s_n. Disconnected nonempty graphs give zero.

350270.title: Universal logarithmic-to-linear speed-up conjecture for covering graphs with independent walks
350270.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let a simple random walk on $G$ have cover time $t_{\mathrm{cov}}$, and let $t_{\mathrm{cov}}(k)$ denote the expected time for $k$ independent walks to cover $G$. Define the speed-up by

$$
S^k(G)=\frac{t_{\mathrm{cov}}}{t_{\mathrm{cov}}(k)}.
$$

**Universal speed-up conjecture.** There exist universal constants $C$ and $C'$ such that, for every graph $G$ and every $k$,

$$
C'\log k\leq S^k(G)\leq Ck.
$$

The conjecture predicts that the speed-up from using $k$ independent walks is always at least logarithmic and at most linear in $k$. The source attributes it to Alon, Kozma and collaborators; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
350270.review_depth: Current v3 §1 discrete-time definition, worst initial configurations, Conj1.1.
350270.ordinary_attempt: K2 worst-start cover time is exactly one for any k. Hence S=1 and no positive C prime log k lower bound can hold for unrestricted k.
350270.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Domain/saturation correction only. Positive-constant convention required; bounded-k intended research problem remains unresolved. No credit for this defect.

375665.title: Aydinian–Blinovsky refinement of the MMS conjecture
375665.statement:
Let $n\ge 2$ be an integer. Let $\mathcal{N}_n$ be the family of multisets $P=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ of real numbers satisfying $\sum_{j=1}^n x_j=0$. Choose $\mathbb{I}\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ uniformly at random and define

$$
X_P=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{I}}x_j.
$$

For $i\in[n-1]$, let $H_i\sim\operatorname{Hyp}(n,i,k)$ be a hypergeometric random variable.

**Aydinian–Blinovsky refinement.** For every $k\in[n-1]$ and every $P\in\mathcal{N}_n$,

$$
\mathbb{P}(X_P\ge 0)\ge\min_{i\in[n-1]}\mathbb{P}\left(H_i\ge\frac{ik}{n}\right).
$$

This refines the MMS conjecture and is stated to cover all non-trivial parameter instances. The source gives no resolution status for the refinement, so it is recorded as open.
375665.review_depth: Current v1 Conj1 MMS and Conj2 refinement with two-valued hypergeometric populations.
375665.ordinary_attempt: Two-valued zero-sum populations attain the proposed right-side comparison values. No valid reduction shows arbitrary populations have at least that many nonnegative k-subsets.
375665.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need a global extremizer theorem over arbitrary zero-sum real populations; convexity of the discrete threshold probability is unavailable. No search or solver.

375707.title: The shifted-product nonempty-interior conjecture for product sets
375707.statement:
Let $n\ge 3$ and let $A\subseteq \mathbb R$ be a Borel set. Write $\dim_H A$ for the Hausdorff dimension of $A$. **Shifted-product nonempty-interior conjecture.** For every $n\ge 3$, there exists $\varepsilon_n>0$ such that, if

$$
\dim_H A>\frac{2}{n}-\varepsilon_n,
$$

then there exist $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathbb R$ such that

$$
(t_1+A)(t_2+A)\cdots(t_n+A)
$$

contains a nonempty open interval. This is expected to improve the direct threshold $\dim_H A>2/n$ for Euclidean shifted-product projections, but the conjectured improvement remains open.
375707.review_depth: Current v1 Conj1.3 versus Conj1.7; distinction between linear and shifted-product projections.
375707.ordinary_attempt: Finite-field product covering is not a Borel-real Hausdorff-dimension theorem. Existing threshold 2/n does not supply any positive epsilon improvement.
375707.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need uniform dimension-threshold improvement and nonempty interval, not positive measure alone. Full analytic proof route absent.

376184.title: Bedert–Drăganić–Müyesser–Pavez-Signé random Cayley-graph Hamilton-cycle conjecture
376184.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected Cayley graph of order $n$ and degree $d$. For $p\in[0,1]$, let $G_p$ be the random spanning subgraph obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$.

**Bedert–Drăganić–Müyesser–Pavez-Signé conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every connected Cayley graph $G$ of order $n$ and degree $d$, the condition

$$
p\ge C\frac{\log n}{d}
$$

implies that $G_p$ has a Hamilton cycle with high probability.

This is a random analogue of the Cayley-graph Hamilton-cycle conjecture. The paper presents it as an open problem and proves related matching and $2$-factor consequences for the larger class of connected vertex-transitive host graphs.

376184.ordinary_attempt: Perfect matching or a 2-factor does not give a Hamilton cycle; joining cycles while retaining random-edge probability is the missing structural step.
376184.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Whp is an asymptotic endpoint, not one finite graph witness; no full Cayley-group Hamiltonicity route. Older version/proof bodies unread.

376383.title: The restricted density polynomial Hales–Jewett conjecture
376383.statement:
For $d\in\mathbb N$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, let $\mathcal P(\{1,\ldots,N\}^d)$ denote the power set of $\{1,\ldots,N\}^d$.

**Restricted density polynomial Hales–Jewett conjecture.** There exists $N=N(d,\delta)\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $S\subseteq\mathcal P(\{1,\ldots,N\}^d)$ satisfying

$$
|S|>\delta 2^{N^d},
$$

there are an $A\in S$ and a non-empty $\gamma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that

$$
A\cap\gamma^d=\emptyset\qquad\text{and}\qquad A\cup\gamma^d\in S.
$$

The paper calls this a restricted form of the density polynomial Hales–Jewett conjecture and discusses it as a possible source of positive recurrence results; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
376383.review_depth: Literal complete finite density statement read; current v1 table of contents, introductory recurrence context only.
376383.ordinary_attempt: d=1 reduces to comparable subsets in a dense Boolean lattice, but arbitrary d requires increments exactly gamma^d and disjointness. A generic combinatorial line does not automatically provide that increment.
376383.exact_gap_or_exclusion: No uniform N(d,delta) proof. Primary conjecture body and restricted appendix proof not reviewed; no clearance from title or abstract.

367137.title: Kadrawi–Levit conjecture on the locations of log-concavity breakdowns in tree independence sequences
367137.statement: Let $T$ be a tree, let $\alpha(T)$ denote its independence number, and let $(a_i)_{i=0}^{\alpha(T)}$ be its independent set sequence. Log-concavity is **broken at $k$** when $a_k^2<a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$. **Kadrawi–Levit's conjecture.** For every $\ell\geq 1$, there is a tree $T=T(\ell)$ for which log-concavity of the independent set sequence is broken at $\alpha(T)-\ell$. This conjecture asks how far from the end of a tree's independent set sequence log-concavity can fail; earlier examples broke log-concavity only at the last possible place, while an ad hoc example broke it at $\alpha(T)-2$.

367771.title: He–Juškevičius–Narayanan–Spiro conjecture for odd planar Rademacher sums
367771.statement:
Let $v_1,\dotsc,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be unit vectors, and let $\varepsilon_1,\dotsc,\varepsilon_n$ be independent random signs, each uniformly distributed in $\{-1,1\}$. **He–Juškevičius–Narayanan–Spiro conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that, for every odd $n$,

$$
\mathbb{P}\!\left[\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n\varepsilon_i v_i\right\|_2\leq 1\right]\geq\frac{c}{n}.
$$

This is the proposed odd-$n$ case of Erdős's conjecture, motivated by the fact that the known obstruction requiring radius $\sqrt{2}$ works only for even $n$; whether the asserted lower bound holds remains open in the supplied text.

368023.title: Altman–Gaujal–Hordijk conjecture on densities of balanced sequences
368023.statement: Let $k\geq 3$, and let $\{r_1,\dots,r_k\}$ be a set of distinct positive reals with $r_1>\dots>r_k>0$. A sequence over a $k$-element set is **balanced** if, for every symbol, the numbers of occurrences in any two contiguous subsequences of equal length differ by at most $1$; its density is the limiting frequency of that symbol. **Altman–Gaujal–Hordijk's conjecture.** A balanced sequence with densities $r_1,\dots,r_k$ exists if and only if $\underline r=(r_1,\dots,r_k)$ is the $(k,2)$-power. The conjecture concerns the characterization of possible density sets for balanced sequences; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

369163.title: The v-number conjecture for crown graphs
369163.statement:
Let $G=C_{n,n}$ with $n \ge 4$. The graph $G$ is the crown graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph on two parts of size $n$ by deleting a perfect matching, and $J_G$ denotes its binomial edge ideal. For $T \in \mathcal{C}(G)$, let $P_T(G)$ be the corresponding prime ideal and let $\operatorname{v}_{P_T(G)}(J_G)$ denote the local v-number of $J_G$ at $P_T(G)$. **The v-number conjecture for crown graphs.** For every $T \in \mathcal{C}(G)$, 
$$
\operatorname{v}_{P_T(G)}(J_G)=4.
$$
 This would establish the expected upper value in the bound $3\leq \operatorname{v}(J_G)\leq 4$ for crown graphs with $n\geq 4$; the case $T=\emptyset$ is already known, while the assertion for every cut-set prime remains open.

370830.title: Lorentzianity conjecture for graph-coloring generating polynomials
370830.statement:

$$
|S(v)|\geq \operatorname{deg}(v)+C
$$

for every $v\in V$, then $p_\varnothing$ is ${\cal C}_\varnothing$-Lorentzian. This conjecture is presented as a consequence suggested by the paper's family of Lorentzian polynomials; the source gives no resolution status.

362090.title: Finite-set approximation of fractional-dilate sum-dilate data
362090.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a fractional dilate, let $N$ be a positive integer, and let $\epsilon>0$.

**Finite-set approximation conjecture.** There exists a finite subset $S$ of the integers such that, for every integer $k$ with $|k|\leq N$,

$$
\left|\frac{\log\norm{\alpha+k\cdot\alpha}}{\log\norm\alpha}-\frac{\log|S+k\cdot S|}{\log|S|}\right|<\epsilon.
$$

This gives a finite-set approximation to the normalized sum-dilate quantities of a fractional dilate, uniformly for the bounded range $|k|\leq N$. The statement is presented among the paper's open questions and is therefore open.

362090.exact_gap_or_exclusion: Need one finite integer set achieving all prescribed log ratios with a proof of uniform error. Fractional-dilate definitions fully audited neither here nor via metadata; no domain defect credited.

362897.title: Existence of cyclic 2-designs in every dimension at least 3
362897.statement: Let a cyclic $t$-design in dimension $d$ be a finite orbit of a unitary acting on quantum states whose decohered probability vectors form a simplex $t$-design. **Cyclic 2-design existence conjecture.** For $d\geq 3$, a cyclic $t$-design exists for $t=1$ or $t=2$. The claim is presented as a corollary of the preceding conjectural lower-bound and monotonicity discussion; cyclic 2-designs are constructively known in the dimensions covered by the explicit construction, but the assertion for every $d\geq 3$ remains open.

363474.title: Kahn–Kim variance conjecture for random matchings in regular linear hypergraphs
363474.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer, let $H$ be an $n$-vertex $d$-regular linear $k$-graph, and let $M$ be a matching chosen uniformly from the set of all matchings of $H$. For a vertex $v$, write $\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})$ for the probability that $M$ does not cover $v$. **Kahn and Kim's conjecture.** For every $v\in V(H)$,

$$
\mathcal{P}_H(\overline{v})=(1+o_d(1))d^{-1/k},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Var}(|M|)=(1+o_d(1))\frac{n}{k^2d^{1/k}}.
$$

The conjecture extends the graph case and predicts both the local uncovered-vertex probability and the variance of the matching size. The first assertion is the earlier Kahn conjecture and is refuted for every $k\geq 3$ by this paper; the variance assertion is not resolved by the supplied text.

363583.title: Immunisation conjecture for fast degree penalisation
363583.statement:
Assume the leading parametrisation of the dynamical random tree model, with $\alpha$ the degree-penalisation exponent, $\kappa$ the degree parameter, $\eta$ the speed parameter, and $\nu_2$ the update parameter. Immunisation means that the critical value satisfies $\lambda_1=\infty$.

**Immunisation conjecture.** If $\alpha\geq 1$, then for every sufficiently small $\kappa>0$ there exists $\nu'=\nu'(\kappa,\eta)$ such that

$$
\lambda_1=\infty
$$

for all $\nu_2<\nu'$.

The conjecture predicts an immunisation phase when the degree-penalisation exponent is at least one and the update parameter is sufficiently small. It is motivated by the absence of exceptionally large effective degrees in this regime; the passage gives no resolution.

363583.ordinary_attempt: Finite trees and finite-time extinction do not imply infinite-volume immunisation for every infection rate. The alpha<1 theorem does not reverse at alpha≥1.

365628.title: The nonzero-solution conjecture for distance-$d$ polynomials of $H(d,3)$
365628.statement:
Let $H(d,3)$ be the Hamming graph on length-$d$ words over an alphabet of size $3$, and let $\Phi_d(H(d,3))$ be the associated system of polynomials. A solution is **all-nonzero** if every variable in it is non-zero. **The nonzero-solution conjecture.** For every integer $d\geq 3$, the system

$$
f=0\quad\text{for }f\in\Phi_d(H(d,3))
$$

has no all-nonzero solution. The conjecture would imply the expected equality $q(H(d,n))=d+1$ for all $d\geq 3$ and $n\geq 3$ via the preceding theorem, while the case $d=2$ is already known from the corollary.

365783.title: The floor-probability bounds conjecture for convex sets
365783.statement:
Let $K$ be a compact convex set with a flat floor over the segment $[0,1]$, and let $Q_K(n)$ denote the corresponding probability that $n$ independent uniformly random points, together with the two endpoints of the floor, are in convex position. Set

$$
t_n=\frac{2^n}{n!(n+1)!},\qquad q_n=\frac{1}{n!(n+1)!}{2n\choose n}.
$$

**Floor-probability bounds conjecture.** For all $n\geq 3$ and all $K\in\operatorname{CCSF}([0,1])$,

$$
t_n\leq Q_K(n)\leq q_n.
$$

The lower and upper bounds generalize the known $n=2$ bounds, with the triangle and square giving the respective benchmark values. The supplied text presents these inequalities as a belief and does not provide a resolution.

366443.title: Ath–Sobel conjecture on sparse uniformly most reliable graphs
366443.statement: Let $\mathcal C_{n,m}$ be the class of connected simple graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, and define its **corank** by $c=m-n+1$. A uniformly most reliable graph (UMRG) is a graph in this class whose reliability is at least that of every other member for every edge-failure probability $\rho\in[0,1]$. **Ath–Sobel conjecture.** If $\mathcal C_{n,m}$ is nonempty, $c\in\{5,6,7,8\}$, and $n\geq 2c-2$, then $\mathcal C_{n,m}$ contains at least one UMRG. The conjecture extends the known characterization for corank at most $4$; the supplied text gives no resolution of the stated cases.
